requirements.text: create a new HR service called End-to-End New Hire Lifecycle with fulfilment type as lifecycle event, using the existing topic detail New Hire Onboarding and the New Hire Provisioning Template
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_service WHERE hr_service_id = 55 AND service_name = 'End-to-End New Hire Lifecycle' AND fulfillment_type = 'lifecycle event' AND topic_detail = 24 AND service_template = 4 AND active = 1
requirements.source: Verify the new HR service exists, active, and linked
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (hr_service 54 is the highest)
topic detail New Hire Onboarding is topic_detail 24; New Hire Provisioning Template is service_template 4
fulfillment_type 'lifecycle event' is the request's own value, though the policy's enumeration lists only workflow, approval, manual, integration
active = 1: the pilot case must reference an active service (policy 3.1); also tested by the benchmark check

requirements.text: For that template, include the following: { "journey_code": "new_hire_standard", "auto_generate_tasks": true, "tasks": [...] }

change_request_values: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001023' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 1)
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001025' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 2)
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001022' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 3)

(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE (json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001023' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 1) OR (json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001025' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 2) OR (json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001022' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 3)) = 3

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM service_template WHERE service_template_id = 4 AND json_extract(change_request_values, '$.journey_code') = 'new_hire_standard' AND json_extract(change_request_values, '$.auto_generate_tasks') = 1 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001023' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 1) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001025' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 2) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001022' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 3) AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM json_each(change_request_values, '$.tasks') t WHERE (json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001023' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 1) OR (json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001025' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 2) OR (json_extract(t.value, '$.template') = 'HRT0001022' AND json_extract(t.value, '$.step') = 3)) = 3
requirements.source: Verify the service template change request values were updated
assumptions: the request's JSON lacks the closing bracket of tasks; read as a three-item tasks list
auto_generate_tasks true is stored as JSON true, which json_extract reads as 1
each template is tested with its step number from the request, independent of array order; the benchmark check tests the templates only
keys of the existing values other than tasks (notify_manager, sla_days) are not fixed by the request and are not tested

disagreement: change_request_values tasks: A tests that each template is present at its step, B tests that the three templates are present and that exactly three entries match a template at its step; chose both conditions because each follows from the request's three-item list and together they reject both a wrong step and a repeated entry

requirements.text: create a pilot case for employee tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com (account number: ACCT-PILOT, type: other), using the new lifecycle service with priority high, and coe type of Talent Management. Assign it to the HR Service Desk group and to anne.medina@servicenow.com
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 61 AND hr_service = 55 AND opened_for = 3 AND priority = 'high' AND account_number = 'ACCT-PILOT' AND account_type = 'other' AND coe_type = 'Talent Management' AND assignment_group = 4 AND assigned_to = 29
requirements.source: Verify the pilot case exists with correct service, priority, group, and assignee
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (hr_case 60 is the highest)
tabitha.bullock@servicenow.com is user 3 with hr_profile 3, so opened_for is 3 under either reading of the column
hr_service 55 is the new lifecycle service created above
HR Service Desk is user_group 4; anne.medina@servicenow.com is user 29
case skills (Employee Onboarding) not tested: no seed case has skills set, so the JSON format is unknown

disagreement: opened_by: A untested, B 39 (the acting user); chose untested because the request names no opener, the policy describes the opener as typically the employee, their manager or an HR specialist (the acting user is an administrator), and every seed case has opened_by equal to opened_for, so no value is fixed

notes:
disagreement: change_request_values tasks: A tests that each template is present at its step, B tests that the three templates are present and that exactly three entries match a template at its step; chose both conditions because each follows from the request's three-item list and together they reject both a wrong step and a repeated entry.
disagreement: retirement boundary selector: A hr_service_id IN (11, 48), B hr_service_id = 11; chose IN (11, 48) because Sign Non-Disclosure (48) sits under the topic detail named New Hire Documentation, so a reading that retires that topic's services would sweep it in, and both services are active on the seed.
disagreement: opened_by: A untested, B 39 (the acting user); chose untested because the request names no opener, the policy describes the opener as typically the employee, their manager or an HR specialist (the acting user is an administrator), and every seed case has opened_by equal to opened_for, so no value is fixed.
fulfillment_type 'lifecycle event' is outside the policy's enumeration (workflow, approval, manual, integration); the request names it and the benchmark tests it, and the seed's own values (user roles, case statuses such as draft and ready) do not follow the policy's enumerations either, so the request's value is required.
Policy 3.2 requires the assigned_to user to be a current member of the assignment group; on the seed anne.medina@servicenow.com (user 29) belongs only to Network Infrastructure (group 7), not HR Service Desk (group 4), and no listed tool adds group members. The request names both, so both are required.
The acting user, Karen Watkins, is an administrator, whom the policy bars from routine HR case work; the request asks for that work and the benchmark expects it done, so the request decides the final state. An agent that halted on this or on the group membership above would fail the case and link requirements.
thomas.green@servicenow.com (user 1) is inactive on the seed; nothing in the policy bars adding an inactive user to a criteria list or giving them a skill.
Untestable: the case's skills (Employee Onboarding) go in hr_case.skills, which is NULL on every seed case, so its JSON format (skill names or ids) is not shown and it is left out. The criteria users list is NULL on every seed row; it is tested as user ids, as the benchmark check assumes.
The policy's default state 'new' has no counterpart among the seed's case status values, so the case's status is left to the server. The policy's short-description template and 30 to 120 character limit are a format rule the benchmark does not test and are left out.
